subject: Joint partner liaison: Redwood telemetry adapter for Datadog/Grafana (pilot proposal)
messages:
From: Amanda Ruiz <amanda@observops.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: joint partner liaison + pilot for Redwood telemetry adapter

Hi Kim / Ben —

Appreciate the quick intro last week. ObservOps runs integration projects between ISVs and observability vendors; we’ve sketched a pragmatic pilot to validate a Redwood telemetry adapter that pushes telemetry into Datadog and Grafana Cloud with minimal config for customers. High-level ask: can Redwood commit a small partner liaison engineering slot (2–3 days/week) and a joint runbook to validate connection patterns, sampling, schemas, and troubleshooting flows?

Why this matters: customers keep asking for reference wiring and a supported flow that covers (1) OTLP ingestion -> Redwood SDK -> Datadog/Grafana pipelines, (2) recommended sampling/attributes for inference telemetry, and (3) operational runbooks for SLO/alert wiring. We believe a 6-week pilot with explicit handoffs will produce a supported adapter and a transfer-to-partner kit.

Attached: pilot SOW v0.1, initial runbook skeleton, architecture diagram (stubs).

Proposed scope (short):
- Week 0: alignment, security checklist, test accounts provisioned
- Weeks 1–3: adapter implementation and integration tests (Datadog metrics + traces, Grafana Loki/Tempo integration tests)
- Week 4: joint customer sandboxes (2 internal demos) + runbook editing
- Week 5–6: stabilization, perf baseline, and handoff pack

Ask / next steps:
1) Can Redwood assign a partner liaison (PM/eng) to own weekly syncs?
2) Confirm legal/compliance guardrails (we flagged minimal access: test API keys, telemetry samples).
3) Quick sync this week to agree comms and responsibilities.

Thanks — happy to adapt the SOW; flagged 40–80 engineering hours on the ObservOps side.

—Amanda Ruiz
Director, Partnerships
ObservOps (partner consultancy)
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Ruiz <amanda@observops.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: joint partner liaison + pilot for Redwood telemetry adapter

Amanda —

Thanks for the clear plan and the SOW draft. This aligns with a few customer asks we’ve been tracking (esp. sampling guidance for inference workloads). I’m copying Ben (partner PM), Laura (marketplace/onboarding), and Karthik (runtime/serving infra) to scope feasibility. Quick notes:

- We can assign a liaison (initially fractional): Ben can take point on PM-side and I’ll carve ~8–12 hours/week of eng time from Karthik’s team for the first three weeks. We should be explicit about SLA for test data access and what keys are needed.
- Security/compliance: any access to production data is off-limits; test API keys and synthetic traces only. Laura, can you confirm the marketplace/contract implications?
- Deliverables: please add a short checklist for compliance artifacts (SOC2 evidence, data retention expectations) in the SOW so Legal can triage quickly.

Suggest scheduling a 30-minute kickoff Thursday 11/19 11:00 PST to align. If that works for your team, I’ll send an invite and attach a cleaned SOW with the compliance checklist placeholder.

Best,
Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Tran <samantha@datadog.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amanda Ruiz <amanda@observops.com>, Kevin Li <kevin@grafana.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: joint partner liaison + pilot for Redwood telemetry adapter

Hi Kim / team —

Thanks for looping Datadog in. We’re supportive of a joint pilot and can provide a sandbox org plus engineering time for two shadow sessions (we’ll help validate metrics/trace mapping and APM labels). A few clarifying points from our side:

1) Sampling strategy: for inference-heavy services we recommend a hybrid sampling approach (head-sampling + adaptive tail-sampling). We can share a short config template to test.
2) Tagging: we need a consistent set of attributes (model_name, request_type, latency_bucket, shard_id). If Redwood can export these attributes via the SDK adapter, we can wire dashboards and alerts more reliably.
3) Rate-limited test keys for logs: Grafana paths sometimes ingest via Loki; we will coordinate with Kevin for Tempo/Loki test streams.

We’ll join the kickoff on 11/19. I’ll paste the sampling config in the first meeting and bring an engineer to the second session.

—Samantha
Samantha Tran
Partner Solutions Engineer, Datadog
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Tran <samantha@datadog.com>, Kevin Li <kevin@grafana.com>, Amanda Ruiz <amanda@observops.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: joint partner liaison + pilot for Redwood telemetry adapter — kickoff confirmed

Thanks everyone — kickoff confirmed for Thu 11/19 11:00 PST (calendar invite sent). Quick agenda so we can be efficient:

1) Introductions + goals (10m): what success looks like for Redwood, Datadog, Grafana, and ObservOps
2) Security & provisioning (10m): test orgs, key scopes, and no-prod assurance (Laura to summarize legal constraints)
3) Technical alignment (20m): sampling template (Samantha), required attributes (Karthik), test streams for Loki/Tempo (Kevin)
4) Timeline & owners (10m): confirm liaison cadence, weekly syncs, SOW signoff owner (Ben), runbook owner (ObservOps)

Action items now:
- Ben: prepare a one-page mutual action plan and include handoff criteria for the end of week 6.
- Laura: add a compliance checklist to the SOW and confirm whether this pilot requires a one-off partner addendum.
- Karthik: draft a short list of attributes we can export from the runtime (model_name, request_id, seq_len, latency_ms).
- Amanda: please update the SOW to include the compliance checklist placeholder and send an editable link to the doc.

Attachments for the kickoff: redwood-datadog-grafana-pilot-sow-v1.pdf (stub), integration-runbook-draft.md (stub), architecture-diagram-v1.png (stub).

Looking forward to a crisp kickoff — I’ll run the first 30 minutes and Ben will take notes for the MAP.

Kim
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
